title: Tasty Mushroom Pasta
subtitle: with Miso, Walnuts and Parmesan
description: Miso isn't just an ingredient for soup – it can bring depth of flavour and a touch of saltiness to plenty of other dishes too. Paired here with earthy mushrooms and walnuts, it makes a great base for this weeknight pasta dish.

steps.text: Cook pasta: Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta in the pan of boiling water for 10 mins or until al dente. Reserve 180ml (¾ cup) cooking water, then drain the pasta and return to the pan.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, thinly slice the mushrooms. Thinly slice the spring onion on an angle, keeping the white and green parts separate. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Finely grate the parmesan. Put the walnuts in a cold medium deep frypan over medium heat. Toast, tossing, for 3-4 mins until evenly golden. Remove from the pan and wipe the pan clean.
Make stock: Crumble 1 stock cube into a heatproof jug. Add the reserved cooking water, miso and 2 tsp soy sauce and stir to dissolve.

Simmer sauce: Heat 20g butter in the cleaned pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms, garlic and white part of the spring onion, stirring occasionally, for 5 mins or until tender. Add the stock and 60ml (¼ cup) milk and stir to combine. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring, for 5 mins or until slightly reduced.

Serve up: Coarsely chop the walnuts. Add the pasta and half the parmesan to the sauce and stir to combine. Taste, then season with pepper. Divide the mushroom pasta among bowls and scatter over the walnuts, remaining parmesan and remaining spring onion. Enjoy!

Did you know?: You've probably heard of miso soup, but miso can be used in so many other ways – in sauces such as this one for pasta, marinades, salad dressings and even desserts. Miso is a thick paste made from fermented soybeans, it has a salty, rich flavour and brings lots of umami to a dish. And because it's a fermented food, it's good for you too.
